answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A harbor delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A karst check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A horizon penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 8171 identities need 8171 bonds of 73 tokens, 39250 dollars of hardware and 21 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
